Russia Strikes Passenger Train in Zaporizhzhia Region, Injuring Conductor — A Russian drone struck a passenger train in the Zaporizhzhia region. Ukrainian Railways (Ukrzaliznytsia) reported that a monitor group issued an early evacuation order, helping to prevent mass casualties, though one conductor sustained light injuries. Passengers were transferred to Zaporizhzhia via buses coordinated by the regional military administration.

Putin’s Ukraine Failure Could Speed Russia’s Breakup, Historian Says — British-Polish historian Norman Davies stated that Vladimir Putin’s attempts to reconstruct the Russian Empire have failed, exposing military weaknesses and reducing Moscow to a vassal state dependent on Beijing. Regarding bilateral tensions between Warsaw and Kyiv, Davies validated Poland’s historical grievances over the World War II-era Volhynia massacres but emphasized that a war for survival is not the appropriate moment

We Joined a Secret Ukrainian Robot Mission to the Front Line — Kyiv Post joined a Ukrainian UGV unit from the 13th Khartiia Brigade on a mission to deliver food and ammunition to front-line positions under the threat of Russian drones.
These unmanned ground vehicles can travel dozens of kilometers, evacuate wounded soldiers and retrieve damaged drones. One of them, nicknamed “Erdogan,” continued operating even after hitting a mine and being struck by an FPV drone.

Ukraine’s Watershed — Donald Trump used this month’s NATO Summit to posture but ultimately backed two major moves: a strike against Iran and long‑delayed Patriot missiles for Ukraine, which faces relentless Russian ballistic attacks. Let’s not forget – Europe’s decades of under‑militarization enabled Russia’s invasion, but Trump’s pressure has finally forced NATO states to strengthen defenses. Licensing Patriots to Kyiv offers a game changing new reality as Ukraine prepares its own long‑range st

How the Brother of Ukraine’s Top Investigator Came to Own 143 Apartments — An investigative report published by several Ukrainian media outlets as part of the "Initiative 143" alleges that Oleksandr Sukhachov, the brother of State Bureau of Investigation (DBR) Director Oleksii Sukhachov, acquired 143 real estate properties in Kharkiv between 2018 and 2020 at prices below market value, some for as little as $932-1,856 – per apartment, not per square meter.

Sanctioned Russian Shadow Fleet Tanker Spills Oil Near Oman Coast — Satellite imagery indicates that the Caroline Bezengi, a sanctioned Russian shadow fleet tanker, is spilling oil in a marine conservation area off the coast of Oman. The vessel, which loaded oil in Novorossiysk, last transmitted its position on June 11. The environmental incident coincides with Ukraine’s ongoing “Operation Molochka,” which aims to disable Russia’s shadow fleet in the Black and Azov Seas without causing ecologica

Finland Restricts Maritime and Air Traffic in Gulf of Finland Over Drone Threat — On July 18, Finland temporarily suspended maritime and air traffic in the eastern Gulf of Finland due to potential drone threats. The Finnish Defense Forces stated that the restrictions, which lasted from 5:45 a.m. to approximately 9:00 a.m. local time, were a preventative measure to ensure civilian safety and prepare for possible drone interceptions. No drones crossed into Finnish territory.

Russian Jet-Powered Drone Strike on Kryvyi Rih Kills 1 Civilian — On Saturday, July 18, a Russian jet-powered Shahed drone struck a critical infrastructure facility in Kryvyi Rih, Dnipropetrovsk region, killing one civilian and injuring others. The strike ignited a fire and prompted an emergency response. This attack occurred amid a broader wave of Russian strikes across southern and central Ukraine on July 17-18.

Ukraine’s Long-Range Sanctions Need Europe’s Support — With Europe consistently reluctant to implement tougher sanctions on Russian oil, Ukraine has taken matters into its own hands and launched its own long-range sanctions against the industry that literally fuels Russia’s war machine.

Russia Plans to Mobilize 500,000 Personnel by Autumn, Prepares for New Fronts — Russia is preparing an autumn mobilization of 500,000 personnel, according to Andriy Kovalenko, head of Ukraine’s Center for Countering Disinformation. Kovalenko stated that some conscripts will be sent to the eastern front within two weeks to address personnel shortages, while others will undergo a month of training to potentially open a new front. This assessment aligns with earlier intelligence reports that Russia

Fedorov’s Dismissal – European Media Assessment — European media outlets analyze the recent dismissal of Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov amid ongoing government reshuffles. Czech and Italian publications highlight Fedorov’s technological approach to warfare, noting that his start-up management style and focus on drone technology created friction with traditional military commanders. Austrian media suggest the dismissal may stem from domestic political competition ahead of potential e

Russian Forces Shift to Low-Altitude, Manually Controlled Drone Strikes to Evade Air Defenses — Russian forces are shifting from mass drone swarms to isolated, complex, manually controlled strikes, according to Ukrainian Presidential Advisor Serhiy Beskrestnov. A recent incident involved a Shahed drone descending to 22 meters to evade radar and interceptors. Early Saturday morning, July 18, Russia launched 90 drones and seven missiles, with Ukrainian air defenses destroying 69 drones and one mis

CIA Director Says AI Drones Reduce Russian Recruits’ Battlefield Lifespan to Minutes — CIA Director John Ratcliffe reported that Ukrainian artificial intelligence-guided drones have reduced the average battlefield survival time of new Russian recruits to 20-30 minutes. Speaking at a defense summit, Ratcliffe noted these cost-effective systems help Ukraine counter Russia’s manpower advantage, as US officials estimate Russian losses at 7,000 soldiers weekly.

Fedorov is emerging as a challenger to Zelensky | Bohdan Nahaylo — The dismissal of Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has triggered public protests and exposed a divide between his technology-focused approach and the traditional methods of Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrsky. Kyiv Post Editor-in-Chief noted that President Volodymyr Zelensky’s decision to side with Syrsky has politically galvanized younger Ukrainians who view Fedorov as a reformer.

Schrödinger’s Elections — Russians are slated to go to the polls from Sept. 18 to 20, during which 450 seats of the Russian Federation’s State Duma will be decided. Whether or not real elections will take place has become an ontological problem akin to the Schrödinger cat paradox of quantum mechanics.

Russian Strikes Target Odesa Port Infrastructure and Foreign Vessels, 1 Dead — On Saturday, July 18, Russian forces struck port infrastructure in the Odesa region, hitting a commercial vessel flying the flag of Antigua and Barbuda. The attack resulted in one death and three injuries, while a secondary strike damaged rescue equipment. The incident marks the second foreign vessel targeted within 24 hours, following a Friday strike on a Marshall Islands-flagged ship

Iran Strikes US Allies in Persian Gulf Following Seventh Wave of US Attacks — On July 18, Iran launched strikes against US allies in the Persian Gulf, targeting infrastructure in Kuwait and Bahrain in response to a seventh wave of US military attacks on Iranian facilities. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps threatened full-scale offensive operations if US strikes continue. US Central Command confirmed targeting Iranian logistics and naval assets.

China Declines to Supply Equipment for Russian Northern Sea Route Fleet — China has declined to supply propulsion and steering systems for Russia’s large-tonnage ice-class vessels due to international sanctions, hindering Moscow’s efforts to develop the Northern Sea Route. Russian shipyards lack the capacity and domestic equipment to build the required Arc7 ice-class tankers. The maritime equipment shortage contrasts with ongoing Russia-China military technology cooperation, where the two nation

Sandra Oudkirk Assumes Duties as US Chargé d’Affaires in Ukraine — Sandra Oudkirk has assumed the role of Chargé d’Affaires at the US Embassy in Kyiv, starting her duties on July 8. A Senior Foreign Service member with over 30 years of diplomatic experience, Oudkirk previously served in roles at the US Department of Defense and as Director of the American Institute in Taiwan. She succeeds Julie Davis, who concluded her diplomatic mission as the acting head of the embassy in Ukraine on June 27.

Zelensky Confirms Strikes on Russian Logistics Hubs in Moscow and Tambov Regions — President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed that Ukrainian forces struck two major Russian logistics hubs in the Moscow and Tambov regions on July 18. The facilities were reportedly used to supply sanctioned components for drone production. The 1st Separate Center of Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces claimed responsibility for the strike on the Wildberries warehouse in the Moscow region. The coordinated attacks also ta

EU Imposes Sanctions on Russian Defense Tech Group ABS Electro — On July 17, the EU imposed sanctions on five companies within the Russian ABS Electro group and its board chair, Iryna Kharisova. The group produces electronic components, including the “Kometa” navigation module used in Shahed drones and Iskander-M missiles. Vladyslav Vlasiuk, Ukraine’s presidential commissioner for sanctions policy, stated that targeting the entire corporate structure complicates Russian efforts to evade sanction

Hungary Blocks Opening of EU Accession Clusters for Ukraine at Council Meeting — During a Council of the EU working group meeting on July 17, Hungary blocked the procedure to open accession negotiation clusters 2 and 3 for Ukraine. Budapest agreed to advance cluster 3 for Moldova, but other member states rejected decoupling the two candidate countries. Consequently, no decision was reached. The working group will revisit the screening results for both nations during its final meeting before the

Russian Drone Strike on Civilian Car in Kherson Injures Five — A Russian drone struck a civilian car in the Korabelnyi district of Kherson on Saturday morning, injuring five people, including a 14-year-old boy. The victims sustained blast trauma and shrapnel wounds. This incident follows a series of Russian strikes across Ukraine on Friday, which targeted a Marshall Islands-flagged vessel in Odesa, an agricultural bus in Marhanets, a UN humanitarian warehouse in Dnipro, and residential areas in

Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces Strike 13 More Russian Shadow Fleet Vessels — Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces struck an additional 13 vessels associated with Russia’s shadow fleet overnight on July 18 in the Black and Azov Seas. The targeted ships included dry cargo vessels, tankers, and floating cranes. This latest strike brings the total number of vessels hit during the 13-day Operation “Molochka” to 172.

Germany and France Sign Agreement on Defense Cooperation and Nuclear Deterrence — German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and French President Emmanuel Macron signed an agreement to integrate conventional military capabilities and missile defense with nuclear deterrence. Germany will participate as an observer in the French nuclear drill, Exercise Poker, as a joint steering group evaluates a potential common defense doctrine. Following the halt of their joint fighter jet and tank programs, the countrie

Ukrainian Drones Strike Oil Depot in Moscow Region and Logistics Hubs — Early Saturday morning, July 18, drone strikes targeted multiple logistics and energy sites across Russia and occupied Crimea. Fires broke out at a Noginsk oil depot in the Moscow region and two major Wildberries logistics complexes in Kotovsk (Tambov region) and Elektrostal (Moscow region). Local authorities in the Tambov region reported the deaths of seven Wildberries employees.

Russian Strikes Target Odesa Port, UN Warehouse in Dnipro, Bus in Marhanets — On Friday, July 17, Russian forces conducted multiple strikes across Ukraine, targeting port infrastructure in the Odesa region, a UN World Food Programme warehouse in Dnipro, and a civilian bus in Marhanets. In Odesa, a Marshall Islands-flagged vessel was damaged, injuring four crew members. In Marhanets, an FPV drone strike on a bus killed one man and injured eight others. The UN reported its Dnipro warehouse was att

Zelensky Appoints Poklad as Acting SBU Head and Beskrestnov as Tech Advisor — President Volodymyr Zelensky signed decrees on July 17 appointing First Deputy Head of the SBU Oleksandr Poklad as acting head of the agency, and Serhiy Beskrestnov as a freelance presidential advisor on technological defense development. Beskrestnov said he declined a position in the new Ministry of Defense due to his professional ties with ousted Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov. The appointments follow a broader go

Russia Strikes Kharkiv, Chernihiv Region, Kills 1, Wounds 21 — Russian armed forces killed one civilian and injured at least 21 others across the Kharkiv and Chernihiv regions on Friday, including eight children. The attacks targeted residential areas in Izium, Kharkiv city, and Novhorod-Siverskyi, damaging civilian infrastructure.

Tusk Welcomes Zelensky’s 5-Point Plan as Poland-Ukraine Tensions Ease — Poland and Ukraine signaled readiness to ease bilateral tensions as Tusk backed Zelensky’s five-point plan focused on diplomacy, archives, exhumations, societal dialogue and historical memory.

Ukraine Marks 12 Years Since MH17 Downing, An Act of Russian Terror — President Volodymyr Zelensky marked the 12th anniversary of the MH17 downing – an act of Russian terror – and urged the world not to turn a blind eye to Russia’s crimes.

Drones Strike Russian-Occupied Crimea, Fire Reported Near Gvardeyskoye Airfield — Russian-occupied Crimea came under an overnight drone attack, with a fire reported near the Gvardeyskoye military airfield and possible strikes around Sevastopol’s Balaklava Thermal Power Plant, according to Krymsky Veter.

Kyiv Placed on Alert Twice Overnight Over Ballistic Missile Threat — Ukraine’s Air Force issued two ballistic missile warnings overnight, prompting Kyiv authorities to urge residents to seek shelter. The second alert was lifted at 2:06 a.m., with no strikes, damage or casualties reported.

Russia Prepares Black Sea Fleet Family Evacuation From Crimea – Leaked Order — Leaked documents published by Void Group indicate that Russian military authorities are collecting information on Black Sea Fleet families who could be evacuated from occupied Crimea. The reported order comes amid intensified Ukrainian strikes.

Former Navalny Accuser Arrested After Turning Against Putin — Russian activist Ilya Remeslo, who previously helped prosecute Kremlin critic Alexei Navalny, has been detained on charges of spreading “fake information” about the military. His arrest follows a dramatic break with the Kremlin, during which he called for Vladimir Putin to stand trial and predicted the Russian leader would be removed in handcuffs.

Russia Continues to Produce Missiles Using Foreign Parts — Authorities say Russia continues building missiles using foreign parts from countries such as Switzerland, China and the US, alongside Russian and Belarusian components, based on the forensic analysis of debris from a Russian strike on Bila Tserkva in May.

Ukraine Pledges to Grant Poland Access on Volhynia Files — President Volodymyr Zelensky announced a five-point plan to strengthen ties with Poland following a recent diplomatic rift. Ukraine agreed to grant additional permits for exhumation of the historical sites, while boosting joint capabilities to advance bilateral ties.

Sybiha Appointed as Acting FM, Khmara as MD Amid Cabinet Reshuffle — New Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi appointed acting ministers of defense and foreign affairs, while announcing a restructuring of several government bodies. He also set a deadline for ministries to submit priority action plans by Aug. 5.

Putin Just GUTTED Russia to Keep His War Alive — At that pace, capturing the remaining Ukrainian-held territory in Donetsk would take another 14 years and millions more Russian casualties explains Kyiv Post Special Correspondent Jason Jay Smart.

Kremlin Denies Interference in Trump’s Election — Kremlin firmly rejected US intelligence claims of Russia’s election interference made by President Trump during his speech at the White House. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov called the allegations of Russia being a threat to America’s voting system unsubstantiated, while China separately denied similar claims.

Russian Orthodox Church Structures Pose as Ukrainian Communities to Influence Refugees — A study by the Institute of National Stability and Security alleges that Russian Orthodox Church structures in Europe are disguising themselves as Ukrainian religious communities to influence Ukrainian refugees. Researchers say the network operates through hundreds of parishes, social initiatives, and Telegram channels that promote pro-Russian narratives.

Naftogaz Names Fedorenko Acting CEO After Koretskyi Becomes Prime Minister — Serhiy Fedorenko, a Naftogaz Group board member with over a decade in the oil and gas industry and a stint as a volunteer in Ukraine's Armed Forces, will lead the company on an acting basis. His immediate mandate: keeping heating-season preparations on pace, securing gas reserves in storage, and repairing infrastructure battered by systematic Russian strikes.

Day Two of Fedorov Protests Sees Hundreds Rally Across Ukraine — Protests supporting Fedorov expanded to several Ukrainian cities. Demonstrators demanded his reinstatement, criticized the lack of explanation for his dismissal, and called on the Verkhovna Rada to return from recess and appoint a new defense minister promptly.

Russia Avoids Mentioning Mobilization Before Autumn’s Elections, Ukraine Says — An officer from Ukraine’s Military Intelligence (HUR) said Russia has avoided talking about mobilization ahead of autumn’s elections, though the risks remain. He added that Russia has existing infrastructure for mobilization – it just needs more “cannon fodder” to fill the training grounds.

Zelensky Offers Former Interior Minister Klymenko National Security and Defense Council Job — Zelensky offered former interior minister Klymenko the position of secretary of Ukraine’s National Security and Defense Council (RNBO) on Friday. Klymenko was originally handpicked to become the new defense minister, but popular protests over the removal of former Defense Minister Fedorov have complicated Zelensky’s plans.

‘Your Buddy’s Gone – Restore Starlink, Musk’: Russians React to Fedorov’s Dismissal — Russia’s official reaction to Mykhailo Fedorov’s ouster was studied indifference. The reaction from its pro-war ecosystem was markedly different: relief, celebration and repeated acknowledgment that the former minister had been an effective enemy.

Trump Accuses China of Interfering in 2020 Election During Prime-Time Address — President Donald Trump accused China of interfering in the 2020 US election during a televised address from the White House, although his claims remain unverified. Critics argued the speech was aimed at casting doubt on the electoral process ahead of the upcoming congressional midterm elections.

Zelensky Offers Taras Kachka Post as Ukraine’s EU Representative — President Volodymyr Zelensky has offered former Deputy Prime Minister for European and Euro-Atlantic Integration Taras Kachka to head Ukraine’s representation to the EU in Brussels. The role would include supporting Ukraine’s accession talks and serving as the country’s trade representative in relations with key partners.

Russia Hails Drop in Beer Imports From ‘Unfriendly Countries’ — Russia said beer imports from “unfriendly countries” fell 36% year on year, while beer consumption rose slightly to 3.1 billion liters in the first half of 2026, state media RIA Novosti reported. The research center behind the data noted, however, that the figures cover all countries outside the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), not just those Russia classifies as “unfriendly.”

Ukraine Knocks Out Tu-95 Bomber Used to Rain Missiles on Ukrainian Cities — Ukraine’s SBU said it destroyed a Tu-95 strategic bomber at Russia’s Engels air base after an 800-km (500-mile) drone strike. Zelensky said the aircraft had been used in missile attacks on Ukraine and called the operation another successful “long-range sanction.”

Putin's Approval Rating Sees Biggest Weekly Drop Since 2022 Amid Fuel Crisis — State-linked polls recorded Putin's sharpest weekly approval decline since 2022, with support falling 5 percentage points. Analysts link the drop to Russia's fuel crisis, weakening consumer confidence, and growing public concern over the war.

Fedorov Ouster Exposes Power Struggle Around Zelensky — Fedorov’s public confrontation with Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrsky, support from military figures and protests across Ukraine have turned a government reshuffle into a serious test of President Volodymyr Zelensky’s authority.

Ukrainian Intel Warns of Russian Campaign to Target Frontline Civilian Logistics — Ukraine’s Military Intelligence (HUR) said Russia’s Rubikon drone unit had been ordered to target civilian gas stations, trucks, buses, and cars in frontline regions in a new campaign, urging residents to remain vigilant, while accusing Russian special services of staging false-flag attacks by striking their own civilians.

Hungary's Former PM Szijjártó to Work for Chinese Carmaker BYD — Former Hungarian Foreign Minister Peter Szijjártó said Wednesday that he resigned from parliament to work for Chinese carmaker BYD as "head of the group's external relations," with the country having negotiated a deal to build a factory in Hungary under his government to dodge EU tariffs.

Anti-Ukrainian Hate Incidents Surge in Poland Amid Online Hostility — Reports of anti-Ukrainian incidents in Poland are increasing, with experts linking the trend to election politics, historical disputes, and Russian disinformation campaigns that seek to undermine relations between the two neighboring countries.

Putin Leading Russia to ‘Chaos’, Anti-War Politician Says — Russian anti-war politician says Putin is steering the country toward chaos as authorities seek to block his election bid through arrest, extremism charges, and a travel ban, underscoring the Kremlin’s widening crackdown on dissent ahead of September’s parliamentary vote.

Ukraine Says It Hit 159 Russian Shadow Fleet Vessels in 12 Days — USF say they struck 159 Russian shadow fleet vessels in 12 days, including 12 ships hit on July 17, aiming to disrupt oil and cargo shipments used to bypass sanctions while avoiding oil spills by disabling rather than sinking the ships.

Busification: Is the Ukraine Army Crisis Real? | Eastern Express — Kyiv Post’s Stefan Korshak explains how Ukraine’s controversial mobilization system is fueling public frustration, why reform is urgently needed, and how the country can strengthen its army without weakening the social cohesion vital to resisting Russia.

Ukraine Strikes Kerch Rail Hub, Russian Vessels as Moscow Rushes to Protect Tankers — Ukraine reportedly struck a key railway hub in occupied Kerch and targeted six Russian tankers overnight. Ukrainian sources say the attacks are forcing Moscow to militarize its “shadow fleet” by deploying troops and air-defense teams aboard commercial vessels.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, July 16, 2026 — Latest from the Institute for the Study of War.

Historic First: Ukrainian Troops to March in Belgium’s National Day Parade — Ukrainian troops will participate in Belgium’s National Day parade for the first time, marking another public display of European military solidarity with Kyiv.

Russia Drops 5 Guided Bombs on Sumy, Hits Civilian Infrastructure — Russia dropped five guided aerial bombs on Sumy overnight, striking civilian infrastructure less than six hours after an earlier attack.

A ‘Gift’ to Moscow: Russian War Bloggers Cheer Dismissal of Ukraine’s Tech Chief — Zelensky named Major General Yevhen Khmara acting defense minister after Fedorov’s dismissal exposed a rift with Ukraine’s military command and sparked nationwide protests.

2 Killed, 8 Wounded in Russian Missile Strike on Odesa — A Russian missile strike on Odesa late Thursday killed two people and wounded eight others, including two children, while damaging several civilian sites.

Ukraine Disables 11 Russian ‘Shadow Fleet’ Vessels in Black Sea and Sea of Azov in a Single Day — Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces disabled 11 Russian shadow fleet vessels on Thursday, bringing the total targeted during Operation “MoLoChKa” to 147.
